Alright, let me think about this year the way I always do.

I been farming these 6 mu for thirty years. Same as my father did. Wheat in winter, maize in summer — that's how it goes here in Quzhou. I don't know all them fancy words the dealer uses, but I know what my land eats.

**Wheat first.** I plant the improved seed — everyone in the village uses the one from the shop now, the old seed don't yield enough. For 6 mu I buy maybe 4 bags of compound fertilizer (the 18-18-18 type, that's what the shop sells most) before plowing. That's about 2 bags per mu for the base. Then when the wheat wakes up in spring, I spread urea — one bag for about 2 mu, so 3 bags total. Better too much than too little. If the wheat turns yellow I'll be eating air next summer. I water three times with my well — once before winter so the roots don't freeze, once when it stands up in spring, and once when the grain is filling. Spray for aphids and the rust — usually twice, maybe three times if the bugs come bad. I rotary till, my neighbor has the machine and charges fair.

**Then maize after the wheat comes off in June.** No time to plow proper, so I just drill it in — no-till like everyone does now. The seed is hybrid, that's all they sell. I put DAP in the row at planting, maybe 15 kg per mu, and then when the maize is knee-high I side-dress urea heavy — 20 kg per mu or so. Maize is hungry, it eats more than wheat. Water once or twice if the summer rain don't come. Spray once for the borer worm.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, maize maybe 550. Same story this year I hope.
